differential cohomology (Yamashita)
What is the motivation for the object $\hat{x}$ that recovers to topological terms in the integral $\int_{M^{n-1}} f^{*} \hat{x}$ that lives inside differential cohomology?
Hint
you want it the integral to be a topological action in a field theory. Using ordinary cohomology classes $x$, one loses all geometric information. If one uses only a differential form, one loses global topology and torsion information. The cohomology class $\hat{x}$ has an underlying topological class, a closed differential form that is usually integral, and a flat and holonomic part. This integral therefore produces a gauge-invariant, geometrically refined topological term. This is what Chern-Simons theory needs.
https://www.ms.u-tokyo.ac.jp/~yasuyuki/yamashita-crest2022-3.pdf
differential cohomology (Yamashita)
How does one motivate the definition of a connection in differential geometry to detect cohomology classes, in particular the first Chern class $c_1(L) = [i \Omega / 2 \pi]$ is in cohomology $H^2(X, \mathbb{Z})$?
Hint
with a connection, one can define the curvature, and recover it up to torsion. A line bundle is a topological object, to compute characteristics via local invariants, one must differentia locally. The de Rham class only sees the real part of the integer Chern class, torsion is invisible to the curvature alone, however, a connection detects the Chern class up to torsion. The torsion is recorded by the holonomy or the information in the flat line bundle.

How does the first Pontrjagin number of 4-manifolds recover Chern-Simons theory?
Hint
Differential Pontrjagin classes can be used to show that $SO(3)$ or $\mathbb{R}P^3$ with the usual metric of constant curvature does not admit a conformal immersion in $\mathbb{R}^4$. See Chern, Shiing Shen; Simons, James Characteristic forms and geometric invariants. Ann. of Math. (2) 99 (1974), 48–69

Page 1 cohomological intersection theory
How does one formulate Poincaré duality for a noncompact oriented smooth manifold of dimension $d$?
Hint
There exists a fundamental class $[X] \in H_d^{\mathrm{BM}}(X)$ in Borel-Moore homology such that the cap product $-\cap [X] \colon H^i(X) \xrightarrow{\sim} H_{d-i}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X)$ is an isomorphism for all $i$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 2 cohomological intersection theory
How does one have a fundamental class for submanifolds?
Hint
For a closed oriented submanifold $i \colon Y \hookrightarrow X$ of dimension $m$, define $[Y]_X := i_*([Y]) \in H_m^{\mathrm{BM}}(X)$ via the proper pushforward along the inclusion.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 2 cohomological intersection theory
How does one define a cohomological Bézout theorem?
Hint
Cup product defines a ring structure on $H^*(X)$. Via Poincaré duality, this induces an intersection product $[Y] \cdot [Z] := \mathrm{PD}^{-1}(\mathrm{PD}([Y]) \cup \mathrm{PD}([Z]))$. If $Y^m$ and $Z^n$ intersect transversely in $X^d$, then $Y \cap Z$ is an oriented submanifold of dimension $m+n-d$ and $[Y] \cdot [Z] = [Y \cap Z]$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 2 cohomological intersection theory
What does Thom's transversality mean in non-transverse case?
Hint
Smooth maps can be homotoped to transverse ones, so non-transverse intersections can be perturbed away. This fails in algebraic geometry because the Zariski topology is rigid and continuous perturbations are not algebraic morphisms; it fails in equivariant geometry because perturbations must respect group actions.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 3 cohomological intersection theory
Classify many Borel-Moore type theories?
Hint
(1) Topological: $H_*^{\mathrm{BM}}(X(\mathbb{C})^{\mathrm{an}})$; (2) $\ell$-adic: $H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(X) = H^{-i}(X, \omega_X)$; (3) Motivic / Chow: $H_{2i}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X, \mathbb{Z}(i)) \cong \mathrm{CH}_i(X)$; (4) $G$-theory: $G_0(X) = K_0(\mathbf{Coh}(X))$; (5) Algebraic cobordism: $\Omega_*(X)$ via Voevodsky's cobordism spectrum $\mathbf{MGL}$, which interpolates between $\mathrm{CH}_*(X)$ and $G_0(X)$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 3 cohomological intersection theory
How does one study $G$-theory?
Hint
As the algebraic $K$-theory of coherent sheaves $K(\mathbf{Coh}(X))$. It behaves as a homology theory with proper pushforwards, whereas $K$-theory of vector bundles $K(\mathbf{Perf}(X))$ behaves like cohomology with arbitrary pullbacks.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 4 cohomological intersection theory
Write down the implication of Chow's moving lemma in Chow homology for the intersection product?
Hint
Any two cycles can be moved into proper intersection, yielding $[Y] \cdot [Z] = \sum_\alpha i(W_\alpha, Y \cdot Z; X) [W_\alpha]$, where the multiplicities $i(W_\alpha, Y \cdot Z; X) = \sum_k (-1)^k \mathrm{length}_{\mathcal{O}_{X, W_\alpha}}(\mathrm{Tor}_k^{\mathcal{O}_{X, W_\alpha}}(\mathcal{O}_{Y, W_\alpha}, \mathcal{O}_{Z, W_\alpha}))$ are given by Serre's Tor-formula.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 4 cohomological intersection theory
Apart from using Chow's moving lemma, state another result one can using derived algebraic geometry to get non-transverse intersection theory?
Hint
Form the derived intersection $Y \times_X^{\mathbf{R}} Z = \mathbf{Spec}_X(\mathcal{O}_Y \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^{\mathbf{L}} \mathcal{O}_Z)$. It is quasi-smooth and carries a virtual fundamental class $[Y \times_X^{\mathbf{R}} Z]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ such that $[Y] \cdot [Z] = [Y \times_X^{\mathbf{R}} Z]^{\mathrm{vir}}$, recovering Serre's Tor-formula without moving cycles.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 4 cohomological intersection theory
What are the sheaf theories of finite type one considers? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
Topological $\mathcal{D}(X^{\mathrm{an}})$, étale $D_{\text{ét}}(X, \Lambda)$, and motivic $\mathcal{DM}(X)$. Invented to provide a stable $\infty$-categorical coefficient system $D(X)$ satisfying the full Grothendieck six-operation formalism.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 5 cohomological intersection theory
State the pushforward and pullback adjunction in the six operation. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
Standard adjunction $f^* \colon D(Y) \rightleftarrows D(X) \colon f_*$ and exceptional adjunction $f_! \colon D(X) \rightleftarrows D(Y) \colon f^!$. Invented because $f^*$ preserves colimits (hence has right adjoint $f_*$) and compactly supported integration $f_!$ preserves colimits (hence has right adjoint $f^!$).
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 5 cohomological intersection theory
What requirement is needed for any morphism for compactly supported variants? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
The morphism $f$ must be compactifiable/of finite type, factoring as an open immersion followed by a proper map $X \xrightarrow{j} \overline{X} \xrightarrow{p} Y$, so $f_! := p_* \circ j_!$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 5 cohomological intersection theory
What are the compatabilities associated with tensor products and internal hom? State these formulas in full. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
Projection formula: $f_!(\mathcal{F} \otimes f^*\mathcal{G}) \simeq f_!(\mathcal{F}) \otimes \mathcal{G}$. Base change formula for Cartesian squares: $g^* f_! \simeq (f')_! (g')^*$ and $f^! g_* \simeq (g')_* (f')^!$. Invented to encode that integration commutes with base change and module actions.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 5 cohomological intersection theory
State the condition and definition for the "forget supports" map
Hint
The canonical transformation $\alpha_f \colon f_! \to f_*$ is defined by compactification; it is an isomorphism if and only if $f$ is proper.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 5 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of a scheme of finite type. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
A scheme covered by finitely many affines $\mathbf{Spec}(A_i)$ with each $A_i$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Invented to formalize geometries cut out by finitely many polynomial equations.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 5 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of the derived global sections of an object in the derived category. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
$\mathbf{R}\Gamma(X, \mathcal{F}) := (a_X)_*(\mathcal{F}) \in D(\mathbf{Spec}(k))$, where $a_X \colon X \to \mathbf{Spec}(k)$ is the structure map. Invented as the right adjoint to the constant pullback functor.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 5 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition for the cohomology of a scheme of finite type over a field $k$ given $a: X \rightarrow \mathrm{Spec}(k)$ for the structural morphism. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
$C^\bullet(X) := (a_X)_*(\mathbf{1}_X)$, with $H^i(X) = \pi_{-i} C^\bullet(X)$. Invented as derived sections of the monoidal unit.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 6 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of a structural morphism. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
The canonical projection $a_X \colon X \to \mathbf{Spec}(k)$, representing $X$ as a family over the base point.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 6 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of a dualising complex for a scheme of finite type in terms of a structural morphism. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
$\omega_X := a_X^!(\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{Spec}(k)})$. Invented as the representing object for the Verdier dual of compactly supported sections.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 6 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of Borel-Moore homology. And the relative version. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
Absolute: $C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(X) := (a_X)_* a_X^!(\mathbf{1}_k) = \mathbf{R}\Gamma(X, \omega_X)$, $H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(X) = H^{-i}(X, \omega_X)$. Relative to $f \colon X \to S$: $C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(X/S) := f_* f^!(\mathbf{1}_S) \in D(S)$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 6 cohomological intersection theory
State the canonical isomorphism in the motivic case using Bloch linearised higher Chow groups. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
$H_{2j}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X_{\mathrm{mot}}, \mathbb{Z}(j)) \cong \mathrm{CH}_j(X)$ and $H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(X_{\mathrm{mot}}, \Lambda(j)) \cong \mathrm{CH}_j(X, i-2j; \Lambda)$, identifying motivic Borel-Moore homology with Bloch's higher Chow complexes.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 6 cohomological intersection theory
Does Borel-Moore homology have proper pushforwards? State the definition of proper pushforwards? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
Yes. For proper $f$, $f_! \simeq f_*$, so the counit $\mathrm{Tr}_f \colon f_* f^! \to \mathrm{id}$ induces $f_* \colon (a_X)_* a_X^! \mathbf{1} \simeq (a_Y)_* f_* f^! a_Y^! \mathbf{1} \to (a_Y)_* a_Y^! \mathbf{1}$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 6 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of a fundamental class for $X$ smooth of relative dimension $d$? Why are these conditions needed? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
By purity, $f^!\mathbf{1}_S \simeq \mathbf{1}_X(d)[2d]$; the fundamental class is the image of $\mathrm{id}$ under $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}_X, \mathbf{1}_X) \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}_X, f^!\mathbf{1}_S(-d)[-2d])$. Smoothness is needed so the cotangent complex is locally free.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 7 cohomological intersection theory
State the conditions and requirements for a Gysin map for relative fundamental class. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
For $f \colon X \to Y$ smooth of dimension $d$, purity gives $f^! \omega_Y \simeq f^* \omega_Y(d)[2d]$, inducing $f^! \colon C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y)(d)[2d] \to C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(X)$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 7 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of a relative Poincare duality isomorphism? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
For smooth $f \colon X \to S$ of dimension $d$, the cap product $-\cap [X/S] \colon f_*(\mathbf{1}_X)(d)[2d] \xrightarrow{\sim} f_* f^!(\mathbf{1}_S) = C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(X/S)$ is an equivalence in $D(S)$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 7 cohomological intersection theory
State the exact distinguished triangle and the conditions for the property of localisation? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
For closed immersion $i \colon Z \hookrightarrow X$ with complement open immersion $j \colon U \hookrightarrow X$, there is a fiber sequence $i_* \omega_Z \to \omega_X \to j_* \omega_U$, yielding the exact localization triangle $C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(Z) \xrightarrow{i_*} C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(X) \xrightarrow{j^*} C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(U) \xrightarrow{+1}$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 7 cohomological intersection theory
State the property of descent for cases of Zariski or Nisnevich covers. What is the homotopy limit diagram? What are the conditions? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
Cohomology satisfies descent: for a hypercover $U_\bullet \to X$, $C^\bullet(X) \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathrm{holim}_{[n] \in \mathbf{\Delta}} C^\bullet(U_n)$. Invented to compute global invariants by gluing local sections.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 7 cohomological intersection theory
State the property of codescent for cases of Zariski or Nisnevich covers. What is the homotopy colimit diagram? What are the conditions? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
Borel-Moore homology satisfies codescent: $\mathrm{hocolim}_{[n] \in \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}}} C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(U_n) \xrightarrow{\sim} C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(X)$ for proper covers or Nisnevich hypercovers. Invented as the homological dual to sheaf descent.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 8 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of a stack? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
A pseudofunctor (or $\infty$-functor) $\mathcal{X} \colon \mathbf{Aff}^{\mathrm{op}} \to \mathbf{Grpd}$ satisfying effective descent along a Grothendieck topology. Invented to parametrize geometric objects with nontrivial automorphisms.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 8 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of an Artin stack? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
A stack $\mathcal{X}$ with representable, smooth diagonal $\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$, admitting a smooth surjective atlas $U \to \mathcal{X}$ from a scheme $U$. Invented to do differential/algebraic geometry on quotient spaces by non-finite groups.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 8 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of a Deligne-Mumford stack? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
A stack admitting an étale surjective atlas $U \to \mathcal{X}$, equivalently having unramified/discrete automorphism groups. Invented to parametrize objects without infinitesimal automorphisms, such as stable curves $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 9 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of a stack for the case of an infinity category? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
An $\infty$-functor $\mathcal{X} \colon \mathbf{CAlg}_k \to \mathcal{S}$ to the $\infty$-category of spaces/$\infty$-groupoids satisfying $\infty$-sheaf descent for the étale topology.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 9 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of the Borel-Moore homology of an Artin stack using infinity stacks? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
For an Artin stack $\mathcal{X}$ presented by a smooth simplicial scheme atlas $U_\bullet \to \mathcal{X}$, $C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(\mathcal{X}) := \mathrm{hocolim}_{[n] \in \mathbf{\Delta}^{\mathrm{op}}} C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(U_n)(-d_n)[-2d_n]$, where $d_n$ is the relative dimension of $U_n \to \mathcal{X}$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 9 cohomological intersection theory
State the definition of the cohomology of an Artin stack using infinity stacks? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
$C^\bullet(\mathcal{X}) := \mathrm{holim}_{[n] \in \mathbf{\Delta}} C^\bullet(U_n) = \mathbf{R}\Gamma(\mathcal{X}, \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{X}})$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 10 cohomological intersection theory
What can one use to resolve objects in some nonabelian categories?
Hint
Simplicial resolutions / simplicial objects in the category to construct nonabelian derived functors in the sense of Quillen.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 10 cohomological intersection theory
What is homotopical algebra?
Hint
Quillen's formalism of model categories and $\infty$-categories that allows doing homological algebra in non-abelian settings by replacing isomorphisms with weak homotopy equivalences.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 10 cohomological intersection theory
How does one compute the Dold-Kan equivalence in the abelian case?
Hint
The functor $N \colon s\mathbf{Ab} \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathrm{Ch}_{\ge 0}(\mathbf{Ab})$ sends a simplicial abelian group $A_\bullet$ to its normalized chain complex $N(A)_n = \bigcap_{i=0}^{n-1} \ker(d_i) \subset A_n$ with differential $d = (-1)^n d_n$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 10 cohomological intersection theory
Define the notion of finite projective objects. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
An object $P$ in an $\infty$-category $\mathcal{C}$ such that $\mathrm{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}(P, -)$ commutes with filtered colimits (finite/compact) and with geometric realizations/reflexive coequalizers (projective).
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 10 cohomological intersection theory
Define rigorously an algebraic category using the definition of enough finite projective objects. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
A category $\mathcal{A}$ generated under filtered colimits and sifted colimits by a small subcategory $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{fp}}$ of finite projective objects.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 10 cohomological intersection theory
Define the nonabelian derived category of an algebraic category $\mathcal{A}$ as free generation under? How does one invent the notion?
Hint
$\mathcal{P}_\Sigma(\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{fp}})$, the free completion of the finite projective objects $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{fp}}$ under sifted colimits / simplicial homotopy colimits.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 10 cohomological intersection theory
Compute using the definition for the derived category of sets
Hint
The finite projective objects in $\mathbf{Set}$ are finite sets; their sifted/simplicial completion is the $\infty$-category of spaces $\mathcal{S} \simeq \mathbf{sSet}[\mathcal{W}^{-1}]$, so the nonabelian derived category of sets is the $\infty$-category of homotopy types.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 10 cohomological intersection theory
Why is it the "good" or "finite projective objects" are the smooth schemes. Define smooth schemes. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
Smooth schemes are locally étale over affine space $\mathbb{A}^n$, meaning their coordinate algebras are retracts of polynomial rings, making them projective generators for derived schemes.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 11 cohomological intersection theory
How does one define the conormal complex for a derived Artin stack?
Hint
For an immersion or morphism $f \colon X \to Y$, the conormal complex is the shifted relative cotangent complex $N^*_{X/Y} := L_{X/Y}[-1]$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 11 cohomological intersection theory
How does one define the normal bundle of a derived Artin stack? What does it parameterise?
Hint
The normal bundle/stack is $\mathbb{N}_{X/Y} := \mathbf{Spec}_X(\mathrm{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_X}(L_{X/Y}[-1])) = \mathbf{V}(N^*_{X/Y})$. It parameterizes derived normal deformations and cosections.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 12 cohomological intersection theory
Define what does it mean for something to be of locally finite presentation?
Hint
A morphism $f \colon X \to Y$ is locally of finite presentation if its functor of points commutes with filtered colimits of commutative rings.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 12 cohomological intersection theory
Define the relative cotangent complex of perfect Tor amplitude less than or equal to 1? Define each term slowly. then all at once
Hint
(1) Perfect: $L_{X/Y}$ is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of vector bundles; (2) Tor amplitude in $[-1, 0]$: for any quasi-coherent module $M$, $H^i(L_{X/Y} \otimes^{\mathbf{L}} M) = 0$ for $i \notin [-1, 0]$; (3) Together: $L_{X/Y}$ is locally represented by a two-term complex of vector bundles $[E_{-1} \to E_0]$ concentrated in degrees $-1$ and $0$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 12 cohomological intersection theory
Define the notion of a quasi-smooth morphism of derived Artin stacks?
Hint
A morphism $f \colon X \to Y$ locally of finite presentation whose relative cotangent complex $L_{X/Y}$ has Tor-amplitude concentrated in $[-1, 0]$ (a derived local complete intersection).
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 13 cohomological intersection theory
State the generalised Thom isomorphism and compute the Gysin map for the projection using the virtual rank
Hint
For a perfect complex $E$ of virtual rank $r$ on $X$, there is a Thom isomorphism $C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(\mathbf{V}(E)) \cong C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(X)(r)[2r]$, making the Gysin map of the zero section $s_0 \colon X \to \mathbf{V}(E)$ an equivalence shifted by the virtual rank.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 13 cohomological intersection theory
Produce the Gysin map for quasi-smooth morphisms of relative virtual dimension using Borel-Moore homology. How does one give rise to the relative virtual fundamental class from this definition?
Hint
Factor $f \colon X \to Y$ through a smooth map followed by the zero section of a vector bundle; the specialized Thom map gives $f^! \colon C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y)(d)[2d] \to C_\bullet^{\mathrm{BM}}(X)$ where $d = \mathrm{virdim}(f)$. The relative virtual class is $[X/Y]^{\mathrm{vir}} := f^!(\mathbf{1}_Y)$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 13 cohomological intersection theory
Why does the virtual fundamental class not satisfy Poincare duality in general?
Hint
Because quasi-smooth derived stacks are generally singular as classical schemes; $L_X$ is not a locally free sheaf concentrated in degree 0, so the purity isomorphism between $f^!$ and $f^*$ fails.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 14 cohomological intersection theory
Compute the tangent bundle of a scheme or a Deligne-Mumford stack
Hint
$T_X = \mathbf{Spec}_X(\mathrm{Sym}_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\Omega_X^1)) = \underline{\mathrm{Spec}}_X(\mathrm{Sym}(L_X))$. For a classical smooth DM stack it is concentrated in degree 0; for a general DM stack it is the dual complex $\mathbb{T}_X = L_X^\vee$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 14 cohomological intersection theory
Define the virtual fundamental class. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
For a quasi-smooth derived stack $X$ with virtual dimension $d$, $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}} := p^!([*]) \in H_{2d}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X, \mathbb{Z}(d))$, where $p \colon X \to \mathbf{Spec}(k)$ is the structure map. Invented to assign an intrinsic cycle class of the expected dimension to moduli spaces with obstruction theories.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 14 cohomological intersection theory
State the functoriality theorem of the virtual fundamental class of derived Artin stacks. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
For composable quasi-smooth morphisms $X \xrightarrow{f} Y \xrightarrow{g} Z$, $(g \circ f)^! = f^! \circ g^!$, hence $[X/Z]^{\mathrm{vir}} = f^!([Y/Z]^{\mathrm{vir}})$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 15 cohomological intersection theory
State the base change theorem of the virtual fundamental class of derived Artin stacks. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
Given a derived Cartesian square with $f$ quasi-smooth, the pullback $f'$ is quasi-smooth with the same virtual dimension, and $g^* f^! \simeq (f')^! (g')^*$, so $g^* [X/Y]^{\mathrm{vir}} = [X'/Y']^{\mathrm{vir}}$.
https://www.preschema.com/lecture-notes/cohdag2022/cohdag2022.pdf
Page 15 cohomological intersection theory
State the excess intersection theorem of the virtual fundamental class of derived Artin stacks. How does one invent the notion?
Hint
If $i \colon Y \hookrightarrow X$ is a classical regular immersion and $Z \hookrightarrow X$ is a submanifold intersecting $Y$ with excess bundle $E = N_{Y/X}|_{Y \cap Z} / N_{Y \cap Z / Z}$, then the derived intersection $Y \times_X^{\mathbf{R}} Z$ has $[Y \times_X^{\mathbf{R}} Z]^{\mathrm{vir}} = c_{\mathrm{top}}(E) \cap [Y \cap Z]$.

What is the formal categorical goal of Fausk-Hu-May in axiomatic six-functor formalisms?
Hint
To systematically isolate the formal categorical machinery of the projection formula and duality isomorphisms from specific geometric contexts, showing how right adjoints $f^!$ or $f_*$ can be identified as twists/shifts of left adjoints $f_!$ or $f^*$ via an intrinsic dualizing object.

six functor formalisms in Wirthmueller contexts.
Why is the right adjoint generally harder to understand than the left adjoint?
Hint
The left adjoint (e.g., free construction, scalar extension, pullback $f^*$, or extension-by-zero $j_!$) is explicitly defined by generators and preserves colimits; its right adjoint (e.g., coextension, pushforward $f_*$, or exceptional pullback $f^!$) is given abstractly via the adjoint functor theorem and requires deep descent/duality theorems to compute.
http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/11/4/11-04.pdf
six functor formalisms in Wirthmueller contexts.
How do Neeman's techniques establish the formal nature of Verdier and Grothendieck isomorphisms?
Hint
Neeman proved that in triangulated and derived categories with Brown representability, the existence of right adjoints $f^!$ and their duality isomorphisms with twisted left adjoints are purely formal consequences of closed symmetric monoidal structures and compactly generated categories.
http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/11/4/11-04.pdf
six functor formalisms in Wirthmueller contexts.
How is the standard pullback-pushforward pair $(f^*, f_*)$ structured in a closed symmetric monoidal category?
Hint
Let $f \colon \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a geometric morphism; the pullback functor $f^* \colon \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ is strong symmetric monoidal ($f^*(Y \otimes_{\mathcal{B}} Z) \cong f^*Y \otimes_{\mathcal{A}} f^*Z$ and $f^*\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{B}} \cong \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{A}}$), and its right adjoint $f_* \colon \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ is lax monoidal with an adjunction $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{A}}(f^*Y, X) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{B}}(Y, f_*X)$.
http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/11/4/11-04.pdf
six functor formalisms in Wirthmueller contexts.
What is the categorical relationship between $(f^*, f_*, f_!, f^!)$ when $f$ is a proper morphism?
Hint
When $f$ is proper, the exceptional pushforward coincides with the ordinary pushforward ($f_! \cong f_*$); consequently, the exceptional pullback $f^!$ is the right adjoint to the right adjoint of pullback, $f^! \colon \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ being right adjoint to $f_* \cong f_!$.
http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/11/4/11-04.pdf
six functor formalisms in Wirthmueller contexts.
What is the Grothendieck context versus the Verdier-Grothendieck context?
Hint
The **Grothendieck context** is an adjoint triple $(f^* \dashv f_* \dashv f^!)$ where $f_*$ has a right adjoint $f^!$ (modeling proper morphisms or global module duality); the **Verdier-Grothendieck context** includes the full four-functor setup $(f_! \dashv f^!)$ and $(f^* \dashv f_*)$ with an isomorphism $f_! \xrightarrow{\sim} f_*$ on proper subcategories.
http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/11/4/11-04.pdf
six functor formalisms in Wirthmueller contexts.
How do extension and coextension of scalars model $f_!$, $f^*$, and $f_*$ in module categories?
Hint
For a ring homomorphism $\phi \colon R \to S$, the forgetful/restriction functor is $f^*$; its left adjoint is extension of scalars $f_!(M) = S \otimes_R M$ (left adjoint/induction), and its right adjoint is coextension of scalars $f_*(M) = \mathrm{Hom}_R(S, M)$ (right adjoint/coinduction). Notice that here $f^*$ is generally not strong monoidal unless $S$ is flat/étale.
http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/11/4/11-04.pdf
six functor formalisms in Wirthmueller contexts.
What is the Wirthmüller context and how did it originate in equivariant topology?
Hint
Originating from Wirthmüller's theorem for compact Lie groups $G/H$, a **Wirthmüller context** is an adjoint triple $(f_! \dashv f^* \dashv f_*)$ where the strong symmetric monoidal pullback $f^*$ has both a left adjoint $f_!$ and a right adjoint $f_*$, together with a natural twist isomorphism $f_!(X) \cong f_*(X \otimes D)$ for a dualizing object $D$.
http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/11/4/11-04.pdf
six functor formalisms in Wirthmueller contexts.
How does strong symmetric monoidality of $f^*$ yield the internal hom adjunction and projection maps?
Hint
Since $f^*$ commutes with $\otimes$, the $(f^* \dashv f_*)$ adjunction formally induces a natural morphism $\pi \colon f_*(X) \otimes Y \to f_*(X \otimes f^*Y)$ and a dual morphism on internal homs $f^* \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathcal{B}}(Y, Z) \to \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathcal{A}}(f^*Y, f^*Z)$ via the Barr-Beck/monad comparison apparatus.
http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/11/4/11-04.pdf
six functor formalisms in Wirthmueller contexts.
State Definition 4.6 of the Projection Formula in the abstract axiomatic context
Hint
In an adjoint setup $(f^* \dashv f_*)$, the **projection formula** is the assertion that the canonical morphism $\pi \colon f_!(X) \otimes_{\mathcal{B}} Y \xrightarrow{\sim} f_!(X \otimes_{\mathcal{A}} f^*Y)$ is a natural isomorphism for all $X \in \mathcal{A}$ and $Y \in \mathcal{B}$.
http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/11/4/11-04.pdf

When does a Wirthmüller context arise in algebra and representation theory?
Hint
When $f^* \colon \mathbf{Mod}_S \to \mathbf{Mod}_R$ is the restriction of scalars along a Frobenius algebra/finite flat map $\phi \colon R \to S$, where extension of scalars $f_!(-) = S \otimes_R -$ is isomorphic to coextension of scalars $f_*(-) = \mathrm{Hom}_R(S, -)$ up to tensoring with the dualizing module $\omega_{S/R}$.
http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/11/4/11-04.pdf
six functor formalisms in Wirthmueller contexts.

Hint
An intrinsic dualizing object $D \in \mathcal{A}$ defines a duality functor $\mathbb{D}(-) = \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(-, D)$; the Chu construction formally completes a closed symmetric monoidal category into a $*$-autonomous category where the Wirthmüller and Grothendieck contexts become dual via $\mathbb{D} \circ f^* \cong f^! \circ \mathbb{D}$.

six functor formalisms in Wirthmueller contexts.
Why is the Projection Formula recognized categorically as Frobenius reciprocity?
Hint
The projection formula is the tensor-categorical generalization of classical Frobenius reciprocity $\mathrm{Ind}(V \otimes \mathrm{Res}(W)) \cong \mathrm{Ind}(V) \otimes W$ for representations; categorically, it states that $f_!$ is an enriched $\mathcal{B}$-module functor.
http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/11/4/11-04.pdf

How does the Projection Formula allow moving target objects and computing Reynolds operators/Haar integrals?
Hint
It allows pullbacks of base objects $f^*Y$ to be factored outside the pushforward integration $f_!(f^*Y \otimes X) \cong Y \otimes f_!(X)$; for $X = \mathbf{1}$, $f_!(f^*Y) \cong Y \otimes f_!(\mathbf{1})$, which identifies the pushforward with a generalized Reynolds averaging operator / integration against the Haar measure $f_!(\mathbf{1})$.

How does one invent quasi-separated schemes?
Hint
Require that the intersection of any two quasi-compact open subschemes is quasi-compact, or equivalently that the diagonal morphism is quasi-compact. Non-quasi-separated schemes arise by gluing infinite-dimensional affine spaces along non-quasi-compact subsets.

What is the geometric motivation for Kähler differentials?
Hint
On a smooth manifold $X$, the tangent space $T_x X$ is the space of $\mathbb{R}$-derivations on $C^\infty(X)$. Dualizing to cotangent vectors and generalizing algebraically yields Kähler differentials as algebraic cotangent modules.
